Prose explains intermittent depression overflow and engineered connections in a plain without a developed hierarchical natural river network.

sources.title: Management Direction Statement for Homathko Estuary Provincial Park
sources.publisher: BC Parks Division, Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, Garibaldi/Sunshine Coast District
sources.actual_material_read: Completed original PDF; front matter, setting/context and access prose; Figures 1 and 2, printed pages 3 and 4, visually inspected. Figure 2 supplies the detailed estuary and river-mouth observation.
sources.publication_independence: A separately authored park-management planning project for the estuary, with its own location/boundary figures and strategic management text. Its substantive map is a bespoke estuary and park-boundary composition, not the stopped Tweedsmuir visitor brochure or DataBC map-service response.
sources.limits: Figure 2 covers the terminal vicinity only. Figure 1 locates the park regionally but does not map the intervening selected river corridor in useful detail. The document explicitly marks several photographs unavailable; those photographs were not used.

correspondence.component_scope: 61508438-opening-laboulaye
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is immediately south of Laboulaye and turns east across its southeastern rural plain. The original basin figure locates this land within the western La Picasa study area, but does not draw a corresponding watercourse from the chosen opening to the Rosales reservoir approach. The system canal entering from farther southwest near reservoir R1 is a different approach and is not substituted.

correspondence.component_scope: 61508438-rosales-reservoir
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward descent crosses the reservoir mapped as R2 west of Rosales and continues into the low country to its south. R2 is a study label for a regulation lagoon. It is not presented as a verified natural hydronym, and its identification does not establish the preceding headward connection.

correspondence.component_scope: 61508438-southern-middle-corridor
correspondence.finding: Beyond the Rosales passage the selection runs east and southeast through depressed agricultural country north and northeast of Villa Rossi, then southwest of Rufino toward the provincial boundary. Figures 1, 2 and 8 distinguish this long southern selection from the engineered corridor farther north through the Leguizamón system and reservoirs R3, R4 and R5. Basin membership and scattered depressions do not establish the selected through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: 61508438-lower-depression-chain
correspondence.finding: The lower selection reaches the reservoir R6 setting south of Rufino, makes a pronounced southern excursion, and turns northeast toward the R7 lagoon group. The study maps establish these local depressions and a managed inter-reservoir canal, but the southern loop and subsequent selected eastward passage are not shown as one continuous corresponding channel. The numbered reservoirs and their connecting works are not a river name.

correspondence.component_scope: 61508438-final-approach
correspondence.finding: West of Aarón Castellanos the selection bends south and east toward the southwestern La Picasa depression, then turns northeast. The research distinguishes a direct channel toward the lake from the southern diversion and pumping works. Neither those nearby engineered routes nor the general eastward basin slope proves the full selected final loop.

correspondence.component_scope: 61508438-actual-terminal
correspondence.finding: The final northeastward portion enters the western La Picasa lake/depression area and its actual endpoint lies within the waterbody depicted and named in the original study-area map. The selected feature stops there. The lake name does not identify the upstream modeled river, and no continuation to the Salado or Paraná is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Western opening, southward bend and long northeastward interior approach
correspondence.finding: The far western opening is outside the detailed study map. No inspected source establishes its channel identity, intervening wetlands or continuous northeastward connection toward the lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Approach to Lago Arari from the southwest
correspondence.finding: The original distinguishes Rio Anajás Mirim, Rio Arari and Lago Arari. These neighboring labels do not establish the selected oblique approach or its chosen entry into the lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Lago Arari passage and first fragment transition
correspondence.finding: Figures 1 and 3 identify Lago Arari and its continuous elongated waterbody. The northward lake interval and transition between the first two selected fragments lie in this same waterbody at ordinary corridor scale. This component is a lake passage, not proof of a uniform river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern lake opening and second fragment transition
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 depicts more than one northern branch, with Rio Jenipapacu named in the vicinity. It does not establish the selected outgoing through-link into the long northern coastal continuation. Neither that label nor broad lake membership resolves the branch selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern channel, direction changes and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The inspected detailed mapping does not cover most of the northern continuation, its lower westward and return turns, or the actual selected terminal. No terminal receiver or named canal is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Tidal, wetland and possible engineered connections
correspondence.finding: The regional prose establishes seasonal interconnectedness as context only. It does not establish the selected western wetland transfers or a specific canal connection north of the lake; contemporary flow direction, navigation and operating conditions are not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and first southeastward connection
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies near the provincial-boundary line. The source begins its depicted tributary farther along the southeastward approach, leaving the actual opening-to-river connection absent. This is an omitted through-link, not a demand for exact banks or a precise headwater vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward bow and return to the southward valley
correspondence.finding: The selected upper bends correspond to the depicted unlabeled tributary line, including its eastern bow and southwestward return. Nearby Saint-Augustin and Matse labels belong to separate main-river geography and are not transferred to this reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Long middle southward corridor and lateral lake-fed joins
correspondence.finding: The source depicts the continuing long southward river line and the lateral lake-fed branches that meet it before its major eastward turn. No lake or tributary name is assigned from proximity, and no reservoir, glacial or managed connector is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward elbow and intermediate tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward elbow and subsequent northeastward and eastward bends follow the continuous depicted river. North- and south-side feeder joins remain distinguishable at this regional scale; the map supplies no supported name for their waters.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward descent toward the lower annotation
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward continuation follows the visible unlabeled river through several bends up to the station annotation area. This source correspondence ends where the printed annotation begins to conceal the watercourse.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower connecting reach beneath station076201 annotation
correspondence.finding: A substantial lower connecting section is covered by the opaque station076201 data box. Short visible pieces on either side do not establish the concealed through-link, and the modeled continuity is not used to fill it.

correspondence.component_scope: Final visible reach and actual receiving-river junction
correspondence.finding: Below the station annotation the final selected reach is visible, approaching and joining the larger north-south river in the Saint-Augustin coastal corridor. This ordinary junction correspondence does not require an exact bank or modern tidal boundary, and it does not prove the tributary name or the hidden upstream connection.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen_northeastern_opening_and_initial_joins
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and its westward-then-southward initial connection fall north of the acquired geological map. No independent source map was inspected for this opening, possible small-waterbody transfers, or the complete connection into the mapped upper valley. Nearby or general river names do not close this gap.

correspondence.component_scope: mapped_upper_valley_and_Tatlayoko_northern_inlet
correspondence.finding: The geological map labels the southward Homathko River in the valley north of Tatlayoko Lake and depicts its connection into the north end of the lake. The mapped valley arrangement corresponds at ordinary corridor scale to the selection immediately above the lake; the map does not cover the entire chosen opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Tatlayoko_Lake_through_passage_and_southern_outlet
correspondence.finding: The original map shows the full long north-south waterbody labelled Tatlayoko Lake, with the Homathko inlet at its northern end and a southern outlet continuing into the labelled Homathko River corridor. The selected north-south lake passage and outlet agree with this mapped arrangement. The lake name is retained as a distinct component rather than applied as a river name.

correspondence.component_scope: intermediate_mountain_corridor_and_tributary_joins
correspondence.finding: The geological map reaches only a short distance south of the Tatlayoko outlet. The long westward and southwestward corridor, its principal tributary junctions, and the later southward-to-southeastward lower course are not continuously covered by the inspected originals. The estuary location figure is too generalized to substitute for this missing corridor evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_estuarine_terminal
correspondence.finding: Figure 2 of the park management statement depicts the labelled Homathko River approaching from the northwest, turning south beside the estuary, and entering Waddington Harbour, explicitly identified as Bute Inlet. Teaquahan River is separately mapped on the eastern side. This river-mouth configuration corresponds to the selected terminal at ordinary estuarine-corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: glacial_reservoir_and_managed_connections
correspondence.finding: The inspected lake passage is mapped as Tatlayoko Lake and river connections. No on-route glacier transfer, reservoir passage or managed diversion is established by the inspected material. Such features cannot be exhaustively excluded in the uncovered opening and mountain intervals, and nearby icefields are not used as evidence of an on-route transfer.
